name: cz-harness
description: An AI-native delivery Harness for FPT project managers. RD-driven, fully traceable, real-time observable. Ships as a Claude Code plugin: 10 role subagents, 21 slash commands, 7 packaged skills, 9 enforcing hooks + 1 cosmetic deliverable-rendering hook, 3 gate profiles, an event-sourced live board, and an HTML-rendered deliverables system for every agent's output (see docs/DELIVERABLES.md).
buildPhase: 0-5 scaffold — see docs/ and §12 of the plan for exit criteria not yet exercised against a real runtime
notes: 1.0.14: bugfix for 1.0.13's auto-load block — its own explanatory comment contained the literal path '~/.claude/projects/*/', whose trailing '*/' prematurely closed the enclosing JS block comment, turning the rest of the comment text into invalid JavaScript and throwing a SyntaxError that silently killed the whole app script (caught only by the page's own frame-runtime error reporter, so it surfaced as a generic 'Uncaught {stack:...}' console entry, not an obvious one). Auto-load, the project-filter dropdown, and even the base sample-data view were all broken as a result — this was caught live: the command reported success and the dropdown appeared to render in one check, but a fresh page load (cache-busted) reproduced the failure, confirming it wasn't transient. Fix: reworded the comment to remove the literal '*/' substring (now 'merges each ~/.claude/projects subfolder's session logs...'); verified with `node --check` against the extracted app <script> block, which now parses clean, and against a live reload showing 'All projects (2)' with 7,075 turns / 33.17M tokens auto-loaded. No functional/behavioral change from 1.0.13's intent — comment text only.

1.0.13: board/usage-monitor.html gains an optional auto-load block (no-op under file://, so opening it directly is unchanged — sample data + manual 'Load Claude log…' picker) that activates only when served over http(s): it fetch()es manifest.json + merged/*.jsonl next to itself, adds a project-filter dropdown to the topbar ('All projects (N)' or any single project), and renders real data immediately with no manual file picking. New board/serve-usage-monitor.sh is the local server that makes this activate: it merges every project's session logs under ~/.claude/projects/*/ into one manifest.json + one merged/<project>.jsonl per project inside ~/.claude/usage-monitor-run/ (top-level *.jsonl files only — each session's sidecar subfolder next to its .jsonl is not additional log data), copies the dashboard there as index.html, (re)starts a 127.0.0.1:8791 python3 http.server, and opens it. commands/usage-monitor.md now runs that script by default, falling back to the original plain file:// open of board/usage-monitor.html if the script is missing or fails. User-requested — they wanted every project's usage visible by just running the command, without manually merging *.jsonl files or clicking through the file picker each time, and asked for the ability to scope the view to a single project. board/usage-monitor.html's own picker-based, sample-data-by-default behavior is preserved byte-for-byte when opened directly; nothing about board/board.html or the cz-harness board/state model changed.

1.0.12: commands/usage-monitor.md now opens a plugin-bundled copy of the dashboard (board/usage-monitor.html, new file) instead of the claude.ai-hosted artifact URL. The dashboard was already a fully static, self-contained HTML/CSS/JS page — sample data by default, an in-page 'Load Claude log…' file picker reading local logs client-side via the browser File API, no fetch() calls, nothing uploaded — so it needed no adaptation to run standalone; it's opened directly as file:// (no local HTTP server, unlike board/board.html, since it has no ../state/board.json fetch to break under file://). This removes the command's dependency on claude.ai hosting/login/network access. The bundled copy is a manual snapshot, not a live mirror: if the hosted artifact at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/cce47a78-3918-4dc6-bbbb-32688a994f2b is edited and republished, board/usage-monitor.html must be re-copied by hand and the plugin version bumped again.

1.0.11: board/board.html gains the Deliverables and Audit & Outcomes tabs 1.0.10 said this plugin didn't ship — ported from the downstream project's own forked board.html referenced in that note, plus a new board/build-audit-index.py (builds gate-records/index.json: the audit trail and outcome/rework-rate metrics both tabs read, alongside deliverables/index.json which hooks/render-deliverable.sh already produces). Deliverables gets Priority/Complexity/Finished back on its own RD table (not Live board's, per 1.0.10's rationale) plus two new columns, Estimate and Actual, sourced from a new gate-records estimate_variance field: hooks/compute-estimate-variance.sh (new) runs automatically at commands/cz-gate.md step 8 on every 'approved' decision, comparing rd/*.md's estimate.expected_h/.pessimistic against the RD's actual build time computed purely from existing telemetry/events.jsonl timestamps for that rd id. Reports both actual_h (raw wall-clock span) and active_h (idle/blocked gaps over LOCK_TTL_S excluded); variance_pct and within_pessimistic_bound are computed against active_h, not actual_h, since an RD estimate is a work-effort guess, not a promise about time spent queued behind max_in_flight or waiting on a human gate. No token estimate/actual: Claude Code hooks have no real per-RD token/cost source (see hooks/emit-telemetry.sh's existing cost_usd comment for the same conclusion) — schemas/gate-record.schema.json documents estimate_variance's fields as an honest reflection of what's actually computed, nothing fabricated. agents/agentops.md's WEEKLY rollup responsibility now includes aggregating variance_pct across a period's accepted RDs to report systematic estimation bias. Verified against a real project's data via temporary symlinks (removed after) before commit; hooks/tests/*.sh suite unaffected (no existing hook's behavior changed).

1.0.10: correction to 1.0.9 — board/board.html's Live board table reverted to its original 6 columns (RD/Module/State/Agent/Time in state/Summary), no Priority/Complexity/Finished columns or priority filter. Rationale: this plugin's shared board.html has no "Deliverables" tab (that concept only exists in at least one downstream project's independently-forked board.html, which has a per-RD Deliverables table alongside its Live board); the user wants the three new columns on a Deliverables-style table, not the generic Live board, and this plugin doesn't ship one to put them on. schemas/rd.schema.json, templates/rd-template.yaml, hooks/project-state.sh, and schemas/board-state.schema.json are UNCHANGED from 1.0.9 — priority/complexity/finished_date remain real state/board.json fields (priority optional/defaults to "medium", complexity/finished_date computed by project-state.sh) available for any downstream project's own board rendering to consume, this plugin's stock board.html just doesn't render them.

1.0.9: user-requested board feature (not an audit finding) — RD table gained Priority, Complexity, and Finished columns. rd.schema.json/rd-template.yaml gained an optional `priority: low|medium|high` field (docs/TRACEABILITY.md and skills/traceability/SKILL.md already named `priority` as content_hash-excluded operational metadata, but it was never actually added to the schema/template until now); hooks/project-state.sh defaults it to "medium" for any RD without the field, so none of a project's existing rd/*.md files need a backfill. Complexity is display-only, not a stored field: project-state.sh buckets the RD's existing estimate.expected_h (already 0-4h) into low (<=1.5h) / medium (<=3h) / high (>3h). Finished date reuses gate-records/<id>-gate.json's gate_decision.timestamp, already read by project-state.sh for accepted-state time_in_state_s but previously discarded afterward — now also exposed as finished_date (null until accepted). board-state.schema.json documents all three new rds[] fields; board.html adds the two new columns plus a static low/medium/high priority filter (module/state filters stay dynamically populated since those value sets are open-ended; priority's is a fixed enum).

1.0.8: closed all 5 remaining Minor audit findings (N2-N5; N1 is a deliberate WONT-FIX, both extra commands kept by user decision) plus one incidentally-discovered bug: gates.yaml's module_overrides example now has an inert-by-design comment (N2); risk-gov.md's 'L0-L5' corrected to 'L0-L4' and cz-risk.md's invented A/B/C leash scale replaced with the real A/A+ vocabulary used everywhere else, including two incidental 'leash B' references in cz-viva.md/viva-prep/SKILL.md (N3); LIGHTWEIGHT-MODE.md's dangling /cz:trace reference fixed to the real command after a full-plugin sweep for other dangling command references found none (N4); gate-record.schema.json rewritten as a oneOf over the 3 real shapes actually used in production (flat phase-level, flat RD-level DOR, nested RD-level review-gate), mechanically validated against all 26 real gate-records/*.json files with 0 failures (N5). Separately: commands/cz-gate.md, skills/gate-engine/SKILL.md, and docs/OPERATOR-GUIDE.md had the gate-2 security-review trigger backwards ('leash=A' instead of 'leash=A+') — found and fixed alongside N3's related cz-risk.md fix; full-plugin grep confirms no remaining instances of the reversed condition. Full hooks/tests/*.sh suite (8 scripts, 73 assertions) re-run after every fix in this round — all pass, no regressions.

1.0.7: full audit pass against Plugin/CZ-HARNESS-PLAN-v0.4.md (see Plugin/CZ-HARNESS-AUDIT-2026-07-29.md for complete findings/fix log). All 9 Critical and 7 Major findings fixed and functionally verified (hooks/tests/*.sh — 8 scripts, 73 assertions, all pass): guard-secrets.sh's grep flag-misparse fail-open on private keys (C2); detect-hazard.sh's BSD-sed bug that silently disabled ALL hazard-path escalation (C1); cz-rd.md auto-committing RD splits with no human step by default (C3); guard-rd-freeze.sh's TC-staleness check being dead code against a sidecar mechanism nothing wrote (C4); contaminated state/telemetry/rd/ shipped inside the plugin package plus the CZ_ROOT-silently-falls-back-to-pwd root cause, now fails loudly instead (C5); guard-red-before-green.sh's cwd-relative red-log path bug, same root cause (M1); rd/*.yaml vs rd/*.md drift across 4 agents' tool grants plus 8 more files found in a full sweep (M2); the entirely-missing skills/ directory, now 7 real skills (C6); telemetry events not conforming to their own schema, reconciled at both the schema and emitter layer (C7); board cost_usd rollup, honestly null until a real cost source exists (C8); OPERATOR-GUIDE.md describing a fictional command/state set, rewritten from the real hook/command source (C9); the board-projection-from-telemetry-alone claim corrected to describe the real hybrid design (M5); board.html's missing leash badge and draft strip row (M6); agentops's append-only guarantee, now a byte-prefix hook check instead of prose (M3); outer-pipeline step ordering, now a real hook instead of prompt-only (M4); RD-GUIDE.md's non-schema-valid estimate/ac field names (M7). Five Minor items remain open (see audit file N1-N5). A pre-fix snapshot is kept at Plugin/_backups/cz-harness-1.0.5-phase0-pre-audit-fixes/.
This plugin defines the CONTRACTS (schemas, config, hook scripts, agent/command definitions, board) for CZ-Harness.

Per-project runtime state (rd/*.md — Markdown with a YAML frontmatter block, not bare *.yaml — tests/**, evidence/, gate-records/, deliverables/, telemetry/events.jsonl, state/) lives in the PROJECT repo that installs this plugin, not in the plugin itself.

deliverables/ is where every agent's narrative output lives (SCOPE/SPEC/ARCH/RISK/reviews/RTM/WEEKLY/CASE-STUDY/...), each auto-rendered to HTML via hooks/render-deliverable.sh using templates/deliverables/style.css + page.html.tmpl. See docs/DELIVERABLES.md.
Test runner target for the red/green hooks: pytest (decision recorded 2026-07-27). Other runners are adapters — see hooks/lib/test-runner-adapter.sh.

Open questions from plan §14 not yet resolved: FPT RD-template alignment (Q3), project-code convention for real projects (Q4), language (Q5). Treat rd-template.yaml as provisional until Q3 is answered.

1.0.3: UNDERSTANDING-LOG.md split into deliverables/understanding-log/<phase>.md + deliverables/understanding-log/rd/<rd-id>.md fragments (one writer per file) after a real incident where two RDs' concurrent /cz:dor reviews raced on the single shared file and lost its prior history to a last-write-wins overwrite. UL-<nnn> numbering is now fragment-local. See templates/UNDERSTANDING-LOG.md's header comment and docs/DELIVERABLES.md.

1.0.4: hooks/lib/common.sh gained a CZ_ACTING_AGENT/CZ_ACTIVE_RD 'Identity fallback' section (cz_sole_lock_agent/cz_sole_lock_rd/cz_lock_agent_for_rd/cz_extract_rd_id) since no command/agent runtime actually propagates those env vars across separate tool calls or into Task-dispatched subagents — hooks now resolve identity from state/locks/*.lock instead. guard-red-before-green.sh and guard-rd-freeze.sh were also reordered to try the active claim lock BEFORE grepping the target file's own RD-ID annotations, since a shared file (one file per module) carrying several RDs' annotations previously always resolved to whichever RD's annotation appeared first in the file, not the one actually being worked on — this was caught live when RD-AIBOOTCAMP-005.01a's build shared src/task-model.mjs with the already-green RD-AIBOOTCAMP-002.01a.

1.0.6: skills/ was listed in plan §11's repository layout (7 named skills: rd-decomposition, sdd-loop, gate-engine, traceability, telemetry, devbook, viva-prep) but the directory never existed and plugin.json had no skills field — audit finding C6. Added skills/<name>/SKILL.md for all 7, each self-sufficient (frontmatter description + substantive body pulled from the existing docs/*.md, commands/cz-*.md, plan sections, and config/schema/template files that already define the same territory, not new mechanics), and wired "skills": "./skills" here. Purely additive — no command, hook, agent, or config file changed.

1.0.5: nothing in the harness ever chained one command to the next — agents/sub-pm.md's frontmatter had no Task tool, so the agent documented as 'handing off' to ba/sa/planner/risk-gov/dev/test-designer/ai-reviewer/sec-reviewer/agentops could only compute what should happen next and write state/, leaving a human to invoke every slash command and every RD's /cz:dor -> /cz:build -> /cz:gate cycle by hand (setting human_gates.<phase> to false only removed the pause INSIDE an already-running command; it was never the thing that chained them). sub-pm now has Task and dispatches per its own handoff table, under a new hard rule 6 stating that dispatching is scheduling and never approving — hard rules 1-5 (no src/**, no gate approval, no gates.yaml edit, no committed RD split, hand off when in doubt) are unchanged. New commands/cz-run.md sequences those calls unattended and stops automatically on a true human_gates.<key> (treating an absent human_gates.scope as true — gates.yaml's last unconditional checkpoint), a hard-stop, budgets.per_wave_usd_hard, or exhaustion, reporting the blocking unit and the next manual action; it writes no gate record, flips no gate, and bypasses no hook. Purely additive — no existing command, hook, or one_way_ratchet invariant changed. See docs/OPERATOR-GUIDE.md §3a.
